summary: Tested project editing + project-member management + task/project visibility filtering (backend & frontend) plus full regression. 64/70 backend tests pass. All requested features work as specified (PATCH project, project member CRUD, auto-lead on create, member-scoped GET /projects and GET /tasks, Projects Edit dialog with Details/Members tabs, Sprints project link). 6 failures are NEW authorization gaps I discovered: the project-scoping rule is only applied to the two list endpoints, so GET /sprints and GET /analytics still leak all org data to a plain member, and object-level endpoints (PATCH/DELETE task, task comments, project-member roster) are not scoped at all — a member with zero projects could read comments and PATCH/DELETE a task in a project they don't belong to.

critical.issue: No project-membership check. A plain 'member' who belongs to NO project successfully changed a seeded task's status to 'done' (200) and deleted a task (200) in the Web Redesign project. list_tasks hides them but the mutation endpoints do not. Fix: resolve _get_accessible_project_ids and 403/404 when task.project_id is not accessible.
Any org member can read/post comments on tasks of projects they are not a member of (returned 200). Same missing project scoping.

Not filtered by accessible projects. Member with 0 projects still receives Sprint 1 (name, goal, dates) of the inaccessible Web Redesign project. Visible in UI: Sprints page renders the sprint card with project name '—'.
Not filtered. Member with 0 projects sees total_tasks=6, completion rate, logged minutes and time series for the whole org — contradicts the new visibility rule.
Only calls ensure_member(org). Any org member can enumerate the member roster (name/email/picture) of any project, including ones they cannot see. Should require project membership or manager+.

minor.issue: No deterministic sort (no .sort on created_at). Org order can change between calls, which makes the frontend's default org selection non-deterministic. It also broke test fixtures using orgs[0].
Returns 200 {'ok': true} even when the user is not a project member and even for a non-existent project_id. Consider 404 on deleted_count == 0.

Role check runs before existence check, so a 'member' hitting an unknown project gets 403 rather than 404 (acceptable, noted only). Also no key/uniqueness update path and no validation that color is a hex value.
role is a free-form string; role='superadmin' or any junk is accepted. Should be Literal['member','lead'].
project_id existence is never validated — you can create project_member rows for a non-existent project (returns 200).
Nothing prevents removing the last 'lead'. A project can end up with 0 members, after which no manager can see or manage it (only owner/admin).
There is no DELETE /projects/{id} endpoint, so test/junk projects (e.g. 'Test Prj') accumulate and cannot be cleaned from the UI.

ui_bugs.issue: Empty state is wrong: when projectMembers.length === 0 it renders 'Loading…' permanently. A project with genuinely zero members shows 'Loading…' forever. Needs separate loading vs empty state.
Members tab label renders 'Members (…)' until the tab is first opened (projectMembers.length || '…'), which looks like a broken count on the Details tab.

No error handling anywhere: save(), addMember() and removeMember() have no try/catch or toast. A 403/400 (e.g. 'Already a project member', or manager hitting a restricted action) fails completely silently — the dialog just stays open with no feedback. Also no success toast.

sprint-project-link renders '— ' and is a clickable no-op button when the parent project is not in the user's visible list (member role). Confirmed: clicking it does nothing, no dialog. Should be hidden/disabled.
'New project' button is shown to role='member', but POST returns 403 and save() has no catch — clicking Create silently does nothing. Either hide the button for members or surface the error.
For a member with no projects the copy is 'No projects yet. Create one to get started.' — misleading; they are not allowed to create and projects do exist.
React a11y console warning on every open: "Missing `Description` or `aria-describedby={undefined}` for {DialogContent}". Add DialogDescription.

integration_issues.issue: Works end-to-end (list refreshes correctly), but removal uses window.confirm() instead of an AlertDialog — inconsistent with the shadcn UI used everywhere else.

PATCH + list refresh works, but sibling pages (Tasks/Sprints/Dashboard) hold their own copies of projects and are not invalidated, so a rename made from the Sprints dialog is only reflected after that page's own reload.

issues: Native <input type='color'> swatch is used (browser default picker) instead of a styled/shadcn control — inconsistent with the rest of the design system.
No character/format hint or validation for the color field.
'Add' button is disabled but styled solid indigo, so it reads as enabled (low affordance) until a member is picked.

action_items: CRITICAL: Apply _get_accessible_project_ids scoping to object-level task endpoints — PATCH /tasks/{id}, DELETE /tasks/{id}, GET/POST /tasks/{id}/comments — return 403/404 when the task's project is not accessible.
HIGH: Filter GET /orgs/{org_id}/sprints and GET /orgs/{org_id}/analytics by accessible project ids so a member cannot see sprint/analytics data for projects they don't belong to.
MEDIUM: Restrict GET /projects/{id}/members to project members or manager+.
HIGH: Add try/catch + toast (error and success) to ProjectDialog.save/addMember/removeMember; currently all failures are silent.
MEDIUM: ProjectDialog Members tab — distinguish loading from empty (currently always 'Loading…' at length 0); drop the '(…)' tab count placeholder.
MEDIUM: Sprints page — hide/disable sprint-project-link when the parent project is not in the visible project list (currently a dead button showing '—').
MEDIUM: Hide 'New project' from role='member' on Projects page (or handle the 403).
LOW: Validate ProjectMemberAdd.role as Literal['member','lead']; validate project existence in add_project_member; add deterministic sort to GET /orgs; add DialogDescription for a11y.
critical_code_review_comments: The new visibility rule is enforced only in list_projects and list_tasks. Every other read/write path that touches a project-scoped document (sprints, analytics, task PATCH/DELETE, comments, project member roster) still only calls ensure_member(org_id), so the rule is bypassable. Centralise it: a dependency/helper like `require_project_access(org_id, project_id, user)` used by all project-scoped routes.
add_project_member does not verify the project exists nor constrain `role`, so orphan/invalid project_member rows can be created.
No safeguard against removing the last project lead — the project becomes invisible/unmanageable for manager-role users.
ProjectDialog has zero error state handling, violating the 'every API call needs loading/success/error states' rule.
GET /orgs returns an unsorted list; the frontend picks a default org from it, so org selection is non-deterministic.

rca_of_the_issue: The feature added project-level scoping via _get_accessible_project_ids but wired it into only two handlers (list_projects, list_tasks). All other routes still authorize with ensure_member(org_id, user_id), which merely proves org membership. Reproduction: (1) as owner, DELETE /api/orgs/{org}/projects/{prj}/members/{member_uid} so the member belongs to no project; (2) as that member GET /api/orgs/{org}/tasks -> [] (correct); (3) as that member PATCH /api/orgs/{org}/tasks/{a_task_in_prj} {"status":"done"} -> 200 and the task is actually modified; likewise GET .../tasks/{id}/comments -> 200, GET .../projects/{prj}/members -> 200, GET .../sprints -> full list, GET .../analytics -> org-wide totals. Mitigation: introduce one shared authorization helper that resolves the accessible project id set (None for owner/admin) and call it in every project-scoped route, filtering queries and raising 403/404 for single-object access.
